Entity.Title: School of Nursing and Midwifery, Pakistan

Title: Forging ahead with blended learning
NewsSummary: In mid-November 2014, the School of Nursing and Midwifery conducted an in house faculty development training workshop on blended learning.
NewsContent:
In mid-November 2014, the School of Nursing and Midwifery conducted an in house faculty development training workshop on blended learning. Nineteen SONAM faculty members underwent the intensive two-week workshop aimed at arming them with the knowledge and skills needed to conduct blended learning lessons effectively.

The training which was endorsed by AACME (American Academy of Continuing Medical Education) introduced the faculty to pedagogies that would help them transform the traditional face to face courses into blended learning.

Since 2011, SONAM has been conducting blended learning lessons for students of its Post RN BscN programme in purpose built smart classroom and learning studio.  Beside this handheld devices are also provided to the faculty and students.

At present there is no blended learning programme at the national level for the Post-RN BScN programme as blended learning modalities have still not gained momentum in Pakistan as compared to developed countries. 

The blended learning initiative has transformed pedagogy of teaching and learning as well as improved student learning outcomes. Students are more satisfied as they feel empowered when given the freedom to plan the pace and place of their study, as well as they feel that the interaction with peers and teachers have increased beyond classroom hours.

Today 3 years later 90 per cent of the courses are offered in a blended mode in the Post RN-BScN programme.

Salim Sayani, Director, e health resource Centre, distributed the AACME certificates to the participants. The ceremony was attended by Principals and faculty of other schools of nursing in Karachi. The participants showcased their work of developing blended modules, in a gallery walk to all faculty and visitors.

The participants will begin transforming the degree programme courses into blended mode for the academic year beginning in January 2015, and will work with an assigned mentor, who had experience of offering blended courses in post RN programme. Mr Sayani appreciated SONAM's leadership in faculty capacity building and mentorship in the field of blended learning.
